mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 540i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 540i engine replacement typically costs £2,800-£5,000 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £3,200-£7,000 depending on the generation and specialist. Used engines can be found from £800-£2,200.

mainEntity.name: What engine codes were used in the BMW 540i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 540i has used five main engine codes across its production: M60B40 (E34 4.0L V8), M62B44 (E39 4.4L V8), N62B40 (E60 4.0L V8), N55B30 (F10 3.0L turbo inline-six), and B58B30 (G30 3.0L turbo inline-six). The engine code is stamped on the engine block and can also be verified via your VIN.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW 540i a reliable car?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 540i's reliability depends heavily on the generation. The later N55 and B58 engines are notably more reliable than the earlier V8s. The M62 is known for oil leaks and timing chain guide issues, while the N62 suffers from valve stem seal and cooling system problems. The B58 is BMW's most reliable modern engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW 540i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common issues vary by generation. On M62 V8 engines, timing chain guides and oil leaks are the primary concerns. On N62 V8s, valve stem seal leaks and cooling system failures are notorious. On N55 and B58 engines, gasket leaks and cooling system issues are most common.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 540i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your 540i's generation and condition. A pristine E39 540i (£5,000+) or any G30 540i (£18,000-£40,000) easily justifies replacement. A sub-£4,000 E60 or older example requires careful evaluation - assess the car's overall condition, rust, and interior before committing.

mainEntity.name: Can I still find parts for the BMW 540i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all 540i engine families have strong aftermarket and OEM parts support in the UK. The M62, N62, N55 and B58 are particularly well-supported, with specialists stocking timing components, cooling system parts, gaskets, and full rebuilt units.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 5 Series 540i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 540i was introduced in 1992 as the flagship petrol V8 of the E34 5 Series range, marking BMW's return to V8 power in the executive saloon segment. Over five generations, the 540i badge has been synonymous with effortless V8 performance, evolving from the M60 through the M62 and N62 to the modern turbocharged B58 inline-six, which replaced the V8 in the G30 generation.

milestones.description: E34 540i launched with M60B40 4.0L V8, producing 286hp
E39 540i introduced with M62B44 4.4L V8, 286hp (later M62TÜB44 with VANOS, 286hp)
E60 540i debuts N62B40 4.0L V8, 306hp - first 540i with double-VANOS and Valvetronic
F10 540i launches with N55B30 3.0L turbocharged inline-six, 306hp - the first turbocharged 540i
G30 540i introduces B58B30 3.0L turbocharged inline-six, 340hp - the current generation

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 5 Series 540i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 5 Series 540i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 540i has been powered by five different V8 and inline-six engines across its production run, each with its own character and common issues. While the later N55 and B58 engines are notably more reliable than the earlier V8s, age-related issues affect all generations. A rebuilt 540i engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Why the BMW 5 Series 540i Overheats
problems.affectedModels: BMW 5 Series 540i (all generations, all engine codes)
problems.rootCause: Plastic expansion tanks, water pumps, and thermostats degrade with age and mileage. This is particularly acute on the N62 V8, where cooling system failures are notorious.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement expansion tank, water pump, thermostat, hoses, coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Ideal preventative maintenance on cars over 60k miles
When catastrophic overheating has caused head gasket or bottom-end failure

problems.recommendation: For most BMW 540i owners, preventative cooling system maintenance is the best value approach - particularly on the N62 V8, where cooling system failure is a well-documented weakness. If the engine has overheated badly and suffered head gasket or bottom-end damage, a rebuilt unit with warranty is the safer long-term choice.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW 5 Series 540i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Valve Cover and Oil Filter Housing Gasket Failure
problems.affectedModels: BMW 5 Series 540i (all generations, all engine codes)
problems.rootCause: Rubber gaskets harden with heat cycling. The M62 is particularly notorious - described as "the leakiest engine BMW's ever made". N62 and N55 engines also suffer from valve cover gasket leaks.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of valve cover gasket and/or oil filter housing gasket
repairOptions.longevity: Standard maintenance; recommended when leaks are detected
If oil starvation has caused bearing or timing chain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - assess whether full replacement cost justifies itself against the 540i's current market value.
problems.recommendation: Gasket replacement is routine maintenance on higher-mileage 540i models - particularly important on the M62 where leaks are almost guaranteed. If caught early, this is a straightforward specialist repair.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Guide Failure - M62 and N62 V8 Engines
problems.rootCause: Plastic timing chain guides become brittle with age and heat cycling. Failure can cause chain slack, rattling on startup, and catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps or breaks.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain guides, tensioners, and chain
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative on M62/N62 engines approaching 100k miles
If chain has jumped or guides have failed catastrophically

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On sub-£5,000 E39/E60 540i examples, timing chain guide replacement may represent 20-40% of vehicle value. Assess the car's overall condition before committing.
problems.recommendation: Timing chain guide replacement is a well-known preventative measure on M62 and N62 V8 engines. If you hear rattling on cold startup, have the guides inspected immediately. If the chain has already jumped, a rebuilt engine is typically the most cost-effective route.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 5 Series 540i
finalCta.paragraph: The 540i badge has represented over three decades of BMW V8 and performance engineering excellence. With regular preventative maintenance - particularly cooling system attention, gasket replacement, and timing chain guide inspection on V8 models - your 540i can keep delivering that signature power and refinement for years to come. If replacement is required, EnginesMarket connects you with UK specialists offering rebuilt units with 12-month warranty and nationwide delivery.
